about: Voiceover for the retail media walkthrough. Each step has one or more lines, each one or two sentences and under 10 seconds. A line without a cue plays as the step starts (the first line) or straight after the line before it. A line with a cue plays when the on-screen tip with that title appears; if the line before is still playing, the screen waits for it, so words and screens stay in step. The retailer's name changes to the visitor's company, so lines say 'the retailer'. Run build_voiceover.py after editing; only changed lines are regenerated.

lines.text: The retailer has four screen types: forecourt, shop front, cooler doors and point of sale.
Each one has its own playlist.
First, the forecourt playlist is set to rotate three campaigns, one after another.
New slots belong to Headquarters, for the retailer's own promotions.
Slot one is the one the retailer will sell to brands.
Its owner changes from Headquarters to Advertiser.
One slot in three now earns media revenue, and two keep promoting the retailer's own offers.

steps.title: The same on every screen type

lines.text: Shop front, cooler doors and point of sale get the same setup, in a few clicks.
The retailer decides exactly how much screen time it sells.

lines.cue: Four advertiser slots, ready to sell
lines.text: Four brand partner slots, one on every screen type, are now ready to sell.

steps.title: The advertiser is already set up

lines.text: Frostline Cold Drinks is already set up as a direct advertiser, next to the advertisers synced from DSPs.
Slots are always sold through deals. A brand is never assigned to a slot directly.
This direct deal gives Frostline all of December at a fixed CPM, and it's never sent to a DSP.

steps.title: Put the deal on all four slots

lines.text: The four new brand partner slots start unassigned, so nothing plays in them yet.

lines.cue: The new deal, not on a slot yet
lines.text: Frostline's deal is saved as a draft, ready to place on the slots.
Each slot's list offers DSPs for open auction, and deals.
The retailer picks the Frostline deal for all four.
Direct deals and programmatic demand are managed side by side, in one place.
All four slots now carry the deal, and the deal shows four slots. Then, save the changes.
The forecast plays are for reference only: this is a direct buy at a fixed CPM.
Finalising puts the deal live, and its revenue is reported just like DSP revenue.

lines.cue: Live · direct, not sent to a DSP
lines.text: Every December window on all four screen types is now Frostline's.
Finally, the retailer gives Frostline its own login, so the brand can manage its own campaigns.
Alex gets the Advertiser role, so Alex only ever sees Frostline's campaigns.
The invitation goes out, and the retailer's first brand partner deal is done.

steps.title: Frostline signs in with its own login

lines.text: Alex from Frostline signs in with the login the retailer provided. Frostline can run its own campaigns, or leave them to the retailer.
Everything Alex sees is scoped to Frostline's own campaigns.
To start a new campaign, Alex selects Launch a New Campaign, at the top of the list.
There's no form to fill in. Alex just talks, and the AI campaign agent listens.
As Alex speaks, it captures the campaign name, products, objective, screens and audience.
A whole campaign brief, in the time it takes to describe it.
The agent writes the brief from what Alex said, and from how past campaigns performed.
It's ready in seconds, with nothing typed by hand.
Frostline's deal ID is pre-selected, so the campaign can only use the slots on that deal.
Name, details, products, audience and objective are all filled in.
Only the deal's four screen types are switched on.
Next, the agent writes the headline and copy from the agreed brand guidelines: Frostline's, the retailer's, or an agreed mix of both.
Every word can be edited before any creative is made.
With the copy agreed, the agent generates a creative preview of the first and last frames.
The frames follow the agreed brand guidelines, and draw on what worked best in past campaigns.
Not quite right? Alex asks for a change in plain English, like a brighter background for daytime forecourts.
And the frame is regenerated with the change.
Generate Creative Assets builds the final creative for every screen type: forecourt, shop front, cooler doors and point of sale.
Once the approved campaign runs, its results feed Frostline's future campaigns, closing the loop.
Frostline also wants a second campaign, just for Gold members.
Targeting is set on the campaign's Targeting tab, exactly as the retailer would.
Alex adds a rule: Audience Segments includes Loyalty Gold.
Every option is a drop-down, so there's nothing to type and nothing to get wrong.
Only the data sources, attributes and values the retailer has approved for brands appear here.
The retailer controls 100% of the targeting it shares.
The data stays in the retailer's own cloud. Frostline only ever picks a segment.
A second rule adds purchase history from the retailer's point-of-sale data.
Purchase History includes cold drinks, again picked from a list.
Targeting on real loyalty and sales data is what makes in-store media so valuable, to brands and to the retailer.
Gold members who buy cold drinks match both rules, and Alex saves the targeting with Save Changes.
Saving doesn't submit anything. Send for approval, at the top right, sends the campaign to the retailer.
It's now awaiting approval, with no activation toggle until the retailer approves it.
Every brand campaign needs the retailer's approval before it can play. Frostline's is waiting in Campaign Approval.
One click on Approve Selected, and Frostline's Gold campaign is approved, with its own creative ID.
Once it's approved, the activation toggle appears in place of Send for approval.

steps.title: Emma checks in at the pump

lines.text: Emma, a Gold loyalty member, pulls in to Highway 9 Services.
The retailer's loyalty app welcomes her by name and invites her to check in.
One tap, and she's checked in.

lines.cue: Frostline's offer, in the retailer's app
lines.text: Frostline's Gold offer is first in her app.
Her check-in links to what the retailer already knows: her loyalty tier and what she buys.
She matches both of Frostline's rules, in real time.
Every screen rotates three campaigns: two for the retailer, and the brand partner slot.
Most shoppers see Frostline's standard creative in that slot.
But not Emma.
Recognised at the pump, she sees Frostline's Gold version, personalised for her.
At the shop front, the same campaign points her to the cooler doors, right next to her.
At the cooler doors, right where the drinks are: a free upsize on every Frostline.
And at the till, her upsize is applied. One shopper, four screens, one joined-up offer.

steps.title: Booked on all four screen types

lines.text: Behind the scenes, Frostline holds slot one on all four screen types, every day of December.
Each booking carries the default creative and the personalised Gold version, both approved.

steps.title: What the brand partner slots earn

lines.text: Booking revenue shows what the slots earn: every window sold, at Frostline's fixed CPM.
That's over 67 thousand dollars in two weeks, from one slot in three.
